newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat pauses after sharp rise.
newsitem.headline: French wheat pauses after sharp rise.

text.p: French wheat prices were steady on Monday after rising sharply last week on strong export demand, dealers said.
Sellers remained in control but trade was slow overall due to a lack of fresh news, they said.
Wheat into Rouen for March delivery was offered at 895 francs per tonne, the level paid on Friday.
March wheat had added five francs on Friday after the European Union granted 436,500 tonnes of soft wheat at its weekly auction, making the award the largest of the season.
Operators said they were looking for clues to market direction and trying to assess the potential for further price rises.
"We do not know which way the market is heading," one dealer said.

Earlier a European Commission official said the EU may wrap up soft wheat exports for the 1996/97 campaign before the traditional end-April deadline, having already exported substantial volumes. But dealers doubted the warning would depress prices.
"Even if Brussels stops exports, the firm trend is there," one dealer said.
MATIF fob barge wheat futures for May were bid at 925 francs per tonne and offered at 930 francs but there was no trade.
